extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff and legal practitioners handling reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO disciplinary order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-court suspension, describing procedural requirements for contesting the discipline, the imposed sanctions, publication and notice duties, and compliance obligations during suspension and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) Director may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the USPTO Director impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner based on disciplinary action in another jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Notice and Order Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' is mailed to the respondent informing them of the Complaint and the requested discipline. If respondent does not timely contest (see next criterion), the USPTO Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose discipline identical to that imposed by the other jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a timely response establishing a genuine issue of material fact (§ 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must file, within 40 days of the Notice and Order, a response containing all information respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the other jurisdiction would be unwarranted based on any grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the required response is treated as absence of any genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d), permitting imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for a period of six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets the period (six months) and specifies the suspension begins on the date noted in the order (here, the imposed suspension begins on January 22, 2010). The suspension is imposed pursuant to the cited statutory and regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client business and duty to withdraw (§ 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is given limited recognition for thirty (30) days after the date of the Final Order to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this limited-recognition period respondent must take necessary steps to close matters and effectuate withdrawal consistent with the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the thirty (30) days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents adding new matters while the practitioner is winding up existing client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order references § 11.58 as an ongoing obligation during the suspension period (the text of § 11.58 governs professional responsibilities during suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED notice obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order instructs OED to publish the Final Order and to publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; disciplinary decisions are also posted at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires adherence to the reinstatement procedures and requirements set out in § 11.60 when seeking to resume practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner, registration number, length of suspension, the rule violations, and the factual basis for the state suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Suspension should identify the practitioner, state the grounds (here, violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5) and the underlying state Rules of Professional Conduct), summarize the specific misconduct, state the suspension period and effective date, and provide reading-room posting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific misconduct findings (basis for state suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner consented to suspension in Colorado for: (1) failing to follow through on intent to transfer to his trust account the unearned portion of a flat fee deposited into his business account; (2) not providing the client with an accounting of the funds delivered to him; (3) not performing the balance of the work for which the client had paid him; and (4) neglecting the legal matter entrusted to him by the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual findings supported violation of the state Rules of Professional Conduct (here, Rules 1.3 and 1.15(a)(b) and (c)) and are cited as the factual basis for reciprocal discipline under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for the USPTO action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites statutory and regulatory bases authorizing the USPTO Director to impose reciprocal discipline and publish notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and mailing requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.11 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order and Erratum were mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11 and to another address where OED believes respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes a certificate of service with the addresses used and the mailing dates, demonstrating required service procedures for disciplinary documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document accuracy and erratum procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An erratum was issued to correct a typographical/terminology error on page 1: change 'exclusion' to 'suspension'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of an Erratum underscores the need for precise terminology in disciplinary orders and the procedural mechanism to formally correct published orders.
